purpose: Legacy evidence corpus for a clean-model table-candidate shadow experiment. Legacy implementation is evidence, not a design template.

capture.warning: The source table caches contain no Docling package/model/config metadata; docling_version is therefore unknown, not inferred from unrelated bake-off records.

cases.why_selected: A filled-rectangle, short-rule six-column table where Docling inconsistently encodes sibling label groups and the legacy pipeline repairs rowspans, covered subrows, white header text, and inline score styling.

nearest_negative_controls.relationship: Same six-column prompt-injection grammar; split-rowspan promotion must not fire.

cases.why_selected: A ten-page sparse/unruled logical table exercising lost-line extension, paragraph recovery, glyph/style recovery, and continuation-row coalescence at every page seam.

nearest_negative_controls.relationship: Adjacent fragments in the same logical table; extension must not fire on already-complete cells.

cases.why_selected: Two compact numeric-table failures isolate adjacent-cell misjoins and a glued-value-plus-empty-cell split while retaining row-rotation and styling pressure.

nearest_negative_controls.relationship: Adjacent table in the same family: rotation still fires, but misjoin resplitting must not.
First table on the exact same PDF page; split_glued_cells must not fire while the second table does.

cases.why_selected: Linked label cells split at inline-style boundaries create surplus cells on pages 78 and 80; page 79 in the same family is an immediate non-overflow control.

nearest_negative_controls.relationship: Previous fragment of the page-79/80 logical table; merge_overflow_cells must not fire.

history.transform: same-row y-band guard for overflow merge

cases.why_selected: The densest semantic case: one logical row crosses a page seam and contains real lists, follow-on paragraphs, links, footnotes, bold/italic runs, and a deep-link page marker.

nearest_negative_controls.relationship: A similarly sparse two-page table whose row also coalesces at the seam, but contains no source list; cell_lists must remain a no-op.

history.transform: seam marker placement inside merged cell

cases.why_selected: The strongest ruled-table case and a critical negative: an earlier truncated-cell heuristic leaked text across these dense rows; the current ownership guard must keep extension inert while preserving labels and links.

nearest_negative_controls.relationship: Negative control is this case itself for extension; no page may fire extend_truncated_cells. The nearest positive is the page-309 fragment in the welfare mega-table.

history.transform: span-ownership guard after the pages 182-185 cascade failure

auxiliary_controls.purpose: Cross-page concatenation control: fragments merge, but no logical row should coalesce across the seam.

replay.reason: Every selected raw Docling HTML candidate and bbox is copied into a committed fixture slice.
replay.exact_per_page_postprocessing: Replayable when the matching oracle cache is present, or after regenerating PyMuPDF observations from the committed source PDF. No Docling call is required.
replay.exact_accepted_output: Canonical table hashes and line locators are independently validated. Later run.py link-target resolution and serialization explain why logical-shadow HTML hashes are not asserted equal to canonical table hashes.
replay.limitation: The snapshots preserve only the already-flattened bbox plus HTML because that is all the legacy cache retained. They cannot reconstruct the richer Docling TableData that production discarded.

observed_dead_or_historical_only_passes.interpretation: These passes have historical motivations but no selected or corpus-wide current cached candidate changed under them. They must not be blindly ported; recover a historical raw counterexample or delete/retire them after broader proof.
